title: Drake Surprises Karol G’s Houston Crowd With ‘One Dance’ Performance
summary: The rapper joined the Colombian superstar onstage for a performance of his 2016 hit "One Dance"
contentText:
Drake made a surprise appearance at Karol G ‘s concert in Houston on Sunday (Sept. 27), joining the Colombian superstar onstage for a performance of his 2016 hit “ One Dance. “

In fan-shot clips from the show, both artists appeared dressed in black, with Drake taking the mic on “One Dance” as Karol G danced beside him before the two moved in close, drawing roars from the crowd.

The appearance was the latest in a series of moments between the two stars. Drake attended Karol G’s Toronto show in July , appearing on the venue’s Jumbotron, and had publicly nodded to her on record before their team-up, name-checking her on “New Bestie” from his 2026 project Maid of Honour . The pair then released “Ahí” in August, and the single made an immediate mark on Billboard’s Latin charts. It debuted at No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs — Drake’s fourth leader on the tally — and gave him his first career No. 1 on Hot Latin Rhythm Songs, a chart he had never previously topped.

Released in 2016, “One Dance” was a career milestone for Drake. Featuring Nigerian star Wizkid and British singer Kyla, it became his first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 as a lead artist, spent 10 weeks atop the chart and reigned for years as the most-streamed song in Spotify history. It has since become a staple of his unannounced guest spots, including a surprise set at Vybz Kartel’s Toronto concert last year, where he also performed it.

For Karol G, the moment adds to a genre-reshaping run. The Medellín-born star became the first Latina to headline Coachella earlier this year, and her 2023 album Mañana Será Bonito made history as the first all-Spanish-language album by a woman to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

Her 2025 album Tropicoqueta debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and she announced her latest album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto , in July, extending a run that has established her as the most commercially dominant woman in Latin music.
